rapport_notes: Warm, patient, empathetic tone throughout; acknowledged stress and made customer feel at ease.
process_discipline_notes: After asking 'does that make sense?' about the hourly rate/minimum structure, rep continued immediately into move-time discussion instead of holding silence for genuine customer processing.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: I was just calling in regards for your online booking for September 16th. Do you just have a few moments to go over that and make sure that the system provided you an accurate estimate? — asks for time and mentions estimate accuracy, but no explicit time-box or promise of 'accurate quote in return' framing.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: And then do you have any specific concerns or questions besides price that you would like answered on this call? — asked AFTER probing began (unit number, floor level already confirmed in prior lines, though the actual agenda line came early-ish in the call).
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises Hutch concern ('it's really special to me. I just would like it to be well taken care of'). Rep responds: 'Okay. Absolutely.' Then pivots to TV without asking follow-up like 'tell me more about the Hutch' or 'anything else you're concerned about?' TV concern then gets one-layer answer (pad, wrap, TV bag) with no second-layer follow-up.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: we do have the no worries damage coverage. That is included in the hourly rate for your move. Which is our free evaluation coverage included provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages. — covered as part of Stage 2 takeaway (not in response to a Stage 1 concern; the Hutch anxiety was acknowledged but not addressed directly with this answer).
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: the meet your mover feature. A few days before your move, you'll receive a meet your mover email introducing them to helping you ease attention of strainers arriving at your front door — covered in Stage 2 takeaway.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: we do have our on time guarantee we value your time. So we can't make it in the time window that we arranged. We Imed start discounting money of your final bill — covered in Stage 2 takeaway.
evidence_quotes.communication: they will give you a call the day before to confirm the move and they will call you when they're on their way to you as well just so you know you'd like to over communicate — covered in Stage 3 (after estimate).
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: It looks like the system estimated about four hours which I would find accurate. — anchor given (4 hours) but no range ('typical 3–5 hours') and no personalization tied to specific factors (floor, walk distance, box count were discussed but not connected to the estimate logic).
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: once we go over that minimum the time is prorated into fifteen minute increments. — states 15-minute increments but does not explicitly say 'if the crew finishes early, you pay less' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.self_prep_tip: the most important one is how well prepared you are when you get there, if you do have the ability to take some items over in a car alert or two that'll help keep our time down in efficiency up. — clearly stated.
evidence_quotes.does_that_feel_fair_then_silence: Does that make sense? [Customer: Yes, it does.] Okay, perfect and then obviously they're a number of factors... — rep asked but then immediately continued talking without a pause for genuine customer reflection.

top_strength: Rep executed a warm, professional tone and skillfully handled the customer's Hutch and TV concerns with concrete, reassuring solutions (pad-wrap-TV bag system) that built confidence.
coaching_note: Ask 'their agenda' BEFORE any logistics probing (unit number, floor, etc.), and when a customer raises a specific concern like 'my Hutch is special to me,' answer it directly with the relevant differentiator (damage coverage) rather than moving on—that's where Stage 1 differentiator credit lives, not pushed to Stage 2.
